title: Android Back gesture leaks a long press and leaves an item stuck in move mode
environment: Current Android phone build in edit mode; Pixel 10 Pro XL running Android 17.
reproduction_status: Reproduced with true Qt TouchCancel and a continuous native Back gesture on the Android 16/API 36 emulator. Automated before/after regression tests pass with the fix. On 2026-10-29 the user confirmed that the fix works on the affected Android 17 Pixel.
reproduction: Open a shopping list containing items and enter edit mode.
Perform Android's system Back swipe from the screen edge/corner over an item.
Observe that a long press reaches the item and activates item movement while the Back gesture is active.
The item is left in an orphan-like or floating move state, and the user has to drop it into place to recover.
actual: The Android Back gesture leaks a long press to an item in edit mode, activates reordering, and leaves the item stuck in a move state until the user manually drops it.
expected: The system Back gesture must not activate an item long press or reorder operation. Gesture completion, cancellation, or loss of the pointer grab must leave item interaction and visual parenting in a consistent state without requiring a corrective drop.
impact: The user reported a stuck move state requiring manual recovery. Isolated native reproduction also established that the next intended checking swipe could delete the affected item; this data-loss path was observed in automated tests, not reported by the user.
workaround: Manually drop the affected item into place, as reported by the user.
source_notes: Qt 6.12 can emit UngrabPassive for TouchCancel with a non-Released point while TapHandler.pressed remains true. Its hold timer can subsequently emit longPressed with point.id == -1.

Ignoring only that late callback prevents the orphan but leaves the recognizer unable to handle the next deliberate long press. Reload only the stale cancelled TapHandler after event delivery; keep its external longPressActive state on the Loader.
A cancelled exclusive swipe can emit UngrabExclusive without a release. SwipeHandler must return the row without checking or deleting it for non-Released points and CancelGrabExclusive.
Keep ordinary grab transfers intact: resetting every onCanceled would interrupt deliberate long-press reordering. The normal reorder control and first post-cancellation reorder both pass.

The earlier multi-command shell motion probe was replaced by a test-only Java injector preserving one pointer and one downTime. Native completion/cancellation, row parenting and the very first subsequent interaction are checked.
acceptance_criteria: Starting an Android Back swipe over a list item in edit mode does not activate long-press movement.
Completing or cancelling the system gesture never leaves a row floating, reparented, highlighted as moving, or stuck with an active drag.
Back navigation does not accidentally check, delete, or reorder an item.
The user can interact normally with the list immediately afterward, without dropping an orphaned item to recover.
Deliberate long-press reordering still works and exits cleanly when completed or interrupted by Back.
Check keyboard-open and keyboard-closed edit states and coordinate the result with UI-006's Back priority.
Reproduce and verify using the physical Android system gesture; ordinary desktop/offscreen pointer tests alone do not cover this interaction.
evidence: User report in the QShopper development chat on 2026-10-28; severity explicitly described as major.

partial_fix.before: With Back navigation implemented but original TextDelegate cleanup, edit mode exited while the held item remained in state drag and parented to ShopView. Adding only onCanceled still failed because disabling the handler did not emit it.
partial_fix.after: Disabled-handler cleanup restores the held row parent when Back leaves edit mode, without requiring a drop. This regression and the deliberate-reordering control pass offscreen and with native Windows rendering.
partial_fix.remaining: Historical UI-006 scope: the user kept the full cancellation fix as the next ticket. UI-007 was then explicitly selected and implemented separately; see implementation below.
partial_fix.reproduction_command: Historical probe; superseded by the continuous-touch matrix command in implementation.
partial_fix.initial_native_evidence: The cancellation probe retained three visible rows but left the milk delegate outside its chooser. The next intended left swipe removed milk instead of checking it. Initial screenshots, XML and SQLite are preserved in out/android-emulator/ui007-cancel-before. This probe was captured during integration; repeat against the final UI-006 APK before selecting the UI-007 fix. Superseded by the valid continuous-touch reproduction in out/android-emulator/ui007-continuous-before, which reproduced the same orphan and accidental deletion.
partial_fix.probe_limitations: The optional multi-segment shell motionevent probe is distinct from the single continuous input swipe used by UI-006's passing Back tests. Individual shell motion calls generate their own downTime, so validate its event timing against a continuous touch source and the physical phone before attributing the entire failure to app cancellation handling.

changes: TextDelegate clears move state on passive ungrab/cancellation and rejects a late long press with an invalid point.
If a cancelled ungrab leaves TapHandler pressed, replace only that recognizer on the next event-loop turn. Do not reload the view or change list data.
SwipeHandler returns cancelled or non-release grabs with Direction.None, preventing accidental selection/deletion.
Retain existing Back priority, intentional reordering, double/single taps, swipe thresholds, gravity and sizing.

regression_tests.name: PointerCancellation::test_cancel (seven data cases)
regression_tests.before: True TouchCancel exposed a stale pressed recognizer and phantom long press; cancelled active swipes could commit actions. The pressed-state assertion also fails the incomplete callback-only guard.
regression_tests.after: Nine records including setup/cleanup pass offscreen and with native Windows rendering. Recovery is asserted before any synthetic release; subsequent long press and swipe work.

regression_tests.name: Native Back gesture completion/cancellation and immediate reorder/swipe recovery
regression_tests.before: Continuous native touch on the UI-006 baseline orphaned a row and the next checking swipe deleted it. Guards alone restored its appearance but failed the first subsequent reorder, despite a passing pre-cancellation reorder control.
regression_tests.after: The original continuous-touch case passes all 14 checks with immediate reorder/restore and checking/correction. The full matrix covers both edges, keyboard states, initial holds of 0/150 ms for cancellation and 150 ms for completion; a one-second hold after recognition exposes stale timers.
regression_tests.timing: Android rejects a Back gesture if the initial stationary hold exceeds its roughly 250 ms recognition timeout. A 1000 ms pre-hold was excluded as an app long press, not treated as a valid Back failure. The valid matrix holds 1000 ms after recognition.

verification: Normal Windows verification: all three CTest entries pass, with 77 UI, 6 keyboard and 52 model records.
Native Windows rendering: all nine PointerCancellation records pass.
Native Android 16/API 36: all 69 full-matrix checks pass, including both edges, keyboard states, completion/cancellation and immediate reorder/swipe recovery.
Shared-key ARM64 debug APK rebuilt; apksigner verified SHA-256 certificate 7c4335c93ec24cb0f92b44ae84ce108180cb299b43ea4e6ef5baafaef7ae029b.
implementation.remaining: None for UI-007. User confirmation on the affected phone complements the automated matrix; broader physical-phone interaction coverage remains QA-001.
implementation.phone_validation: 2026-10-29: user reported "Fix works on phone." No claim of an exhaustive physical-device matrix.
implementation.analyser_followup: The user reported a missing-property warning for Loader.item.enabled: Loader.item is statically QObject. Cast it to TapHandler before changing enabled. qmllint reproduced the warning before the cast and is clean afterward. Evidence: out/windows-agent/tests/ui007-lint-before.txt and ui007-lint-after.txt. Add braces to the new single-line if bodies and record the preference in AGENTS.md.
